# Universal NPC Voice Model Lab

This package contains a single self-contained browser program:

- `Universal_NPC_Voice_Lab.html`

Open that file in a modern browser. The app lets you select one of the 14 NPCs, type any line, choose an emotion regulator setting, adjust the merged slider schema, and speak the line using the NPC's locked biome voice-model.

## How it works

The app is intentionally static and portable. It uses:

1. a locked NPC → biome → fantasy voice-model mapping;
2. browser `speechSynthesis` for offline speech;
3. internal sliders for pitch, timing, stutter, softness, roughness, resonance, formality, vowel flow, consonants, mouth shape, nasality, throat depth, rhythm, pauses, emphasis, warmth, clarity, projection, human variation, and accent strength;
4. influence sliders for race, gender identity, personality/class, biome/accent, uploaded/recorded voice influence, and emotion strength;
5. a locked Apps Script backend hook when available, with automatic browser fallback.

## Important limitation

A static browser HTML file cannot bundle or run full neural TTS checkpoints without a separate engine. This app therefore implements the requested model selection, accent/emotion rules, slider schema, and backend hook in one single HTML file. Browser voices vary by operating system. If a specific language or accent voice is unavailable on a device, the app selects the closest local voice and keeps timing/prosody/accent-shaping rules active.

## Backend note

The backend endpoint is not displayed in the UI. Because this is a client-side single HTML file, any endpoint embedded in JavaScript can still be inspected by someone who opens the source. Real secrecy requires a server-side proxy.

## Files

- `../Universal_NPC_Voice_Lab.html` — the single program file.
- `MANIFEST.md` — package contents.
- `VOICE_MODEL_SELECTION.md` — one selected model per NPC.
- `UNUSED_CODE_AUDIT.md` — audit of uploaded repositories and why they were not copied into the static program.
- `LICENSES_AUDIT.md` — license findings for uploaded source references.
